# apollo_subgraph_api_key (Resource)

Manages a single-target GraphOS subgraph API key. The `key` value is only visible at create time, so this resource preserves it in sensitive Terraform state for Terraform-created resources and intentionally cannot rehydrate it on import or refresh.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "apollo_subgraph_api_key" "products" {
  graph_id      = "inventory"
  variant       = "production"
  subgraph_name = "products"
  name          = "products-router"
}

import {
  to = apollo_subgraph_api_key.products
  id = "inventory:production:products:subgraph-key-123"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `graph_id` (String) Owning graph identifier for the targeted subgraph registration.
- `name` (String) Display name for the API key.
- `subgraph_name` (String) Subgraph that receives the API key.
- `variant` (String) Variant that owns the targeted subgraph registration.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Timestamp when GraphOS created the API key.
- `id` (String) Remote GraphOS API key identifier. Import format: `graph_id:variant:subgraph_name:key_id`.
- `key` (String, Sensitive) Sensitive API key value returned by GraphOS only at creation time. Imported resources and refreshes do not rehydrate this field.
- `last_used_at` (String) Timestamp when GraphOS last observed this API key being used, when available.

## Import

Import an existing single-target subgraph API key with its subgraph identity plus remote key ID:

```terraform
import {
  to = apollo_subgraph_api_key.products
  id = "inventory:production:products:subgraph-key-123"
}
```

## Permissions

- Read, import, refresh, create, update, and delete require Org Admin or Graph Admin access for subgraph API key management.

## Secret Handling

- GraphOS only returns the `key` value when it creates the API key.
- Terraform stores that sensitive value in state for resources it creates.
- Imported resources and later refreshes intentionally leave `key` unset because GraphOS does not re-expose it.

## Boundary

This slice supports exactly one `graph_id:variant:subgraph_name` target tuple per resource. Multi-target subgraph keys, expiration management, and rotation remain out of scope.
